questions.def: 'Never' is used with present perfect to indicate a lack of experience.
questions.question: I have ___ been to Japan. It's on my list.

questions.def: 'Seldom' correctly modifies the verb 'finishes' as a frequency adverb.
questions.question: She ___ finishes her work on time.

questions.def: An adverb ('Fortunately') is needed to modify the entire sentence.
questions.question: ___, I found my keys after searching for an hour.

questions.def: 'Rarely' is the best adverb of frequency in this context.
questions.question: He ___ goes to the gym, maybe once a month.

questions.def: 'Apparently' modifies the sentence, indicating hearsay or assumption.
questions.question: ___, the meeting will be held next week.

questions.def: 'Clearly' modifies 'spoke', requiring an adverb.
questions.question: He spoke ___ enough for everyone to understand.

questions.def: 'Never' begins an inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: ___ have I seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: 'Nearly' is the correct adverb to express approximation.
questions.question: The report is ___ finished; we need another week.

questions.def: 'Truly' modifies the entire sentence, requiring an adverb.
questions.question: ___, the weather has been awful this summer.

questions.def: 'Hardly' expresses a low expectation.
questions.question: I ___ expected to see him here.

questions.def: 'Softly' modifies the verb 'spoke', indicating the manner of speaking.
questions.question: He spoke ___ during the presentation.

questions.def: 'Wisely' modifies 'invested', requiring an adverb.
questions.question: ___, he invested his money in property.

questions.def: 'Utterly' emphasizes the degree of boredom.
questions.question: The film was ___ boring.

questions.def: 'Occasionally' functions as an adverb of frequency.
questions.question: He visits his parents ___.

questions.def: 'Suddenly' modifies 'arrived', requiring an adverb.
questions.question: The storm arrived ___.

questions.def: 'Barely' indicates a minimal degree of feeling well.
questions.question: She has ___ been feeling well lately.

questions.def: 'Incredibly' is an adverb modifying 'delicious'.
questions.question: The food was ___ delicious.

questions.def: 'Patiently' modifies 'waited', requiring an adverb.
questions.question: She waited ___ for the bus.

questions.def: 'Perfectly' clarifies the extent of understanding.
questions.question: He ___ understood the instructions.

questions.def: 'Only' limits the frequency of visits.
questions.question: They visit us ___ now and then.

questions.def: 'Happily' modifies 'danced', requiring an adverb.
questions.question: They danced ___ at the party.

questions.def: 'Rarely' indicates an infrequent occurrence.
questions.question: She ___ arrives on time; it's unusual.

questions.def: 'Loudly' modifies 'spoke', indicating the manner of speaking.
questions.question: He spoke ___ to be heard.

questions.def: Adverbs of degree (almost) precede adverbs of manner (completely).
questions.question: She has almost ___ finished the report.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency (rarely) usually go before the main verb.
questions.question: I have ___ seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: Adverbs of manner (naturally) go before the verb for emphasis.
questions.question: He ___ fluent French naturally.

questions.def: Sentence adverbs (Officially) modify the whole sentence's meaning.
questions.question: ___, the meeting will start at 10 AM.

questions.def: An adverb (exceptionally) is needed to modify another adverb (well).
questions.question: She plays the piano ___ well.

questions.def: Adverbs of time (eventually) go before the main verb for emphasis.
questions.question: I ___ what you meant eventually.

questions.def: Adverbs like 'never' usually precede the main verb or auxiliary verb.
questions.question: They have ___ been to Italy, only France.
